record.original_question: Find a perfect cube such that adding 1 dirham to it produces another perfect cube.

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Find a cube such that, when one dirham is added to it, the result is another perfect cube.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Determine all positive rational numbers $x$ such that both $x^3$ and $x^3+1$ are cubes of positive rational numbers; equivalently, find all pairs $(x,y)$ of positive rationals satisfying
$$y^3 = x^3 + 1.$$
Decide whether such a pair exists, and if so exhibit one; otherwise prove that no positive rational solution exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The equation y^3 - x^3 = 1 has no solutions in positive rationals (or positive integers). This follows from Fermat's classical proof of the impossibility of x^3 + z^3 = y^3 in nonzero integers (the case n=3 of Fermat's Last Theorem), with the only integer solutions to y^3 = x^3 + 1 being the trivial (x,y) ∈ {(0,1),(−1,0)}. Hence the problem is fully resolved: no such cube exists.

status_evidence.title: Fermat's Last Theorem for n=3
status_evidence.snippet: Euler (and earlier Fermat) proved that x^3 + y^3 = z^3 has no solutions in nonzero integers.
status_evidence.claim: y^3 - x^3 = 1 has no nontrivial integer/rational solutions, by the n=3 case of Fermat's Last Theorem.
